threads.body: Patterns with multiple `*` segments compile to chained greedy `.*` expressions. Java's backtracking regex engine can take polynomial/exponential time on a non-match (for example, `*a*a*a*a*a*b` against a long run of `a`s), and `matches()` is expected to run for every captured value. Please use a linear-time glob matcher (or otherwise guarantee bounded matching time) so a configured selector cannot stall instrumentation threads.

replies.body: Fixed in `8302fc3583e` by replacing regex matching with an iterative, code-point-aware glob matcher. It uses no recursion or regex backtracking; each retry consumes one input code point, which bounds worst-case work to O(pattern length × value length), with no per-match allocation. I also added an adversarial chained-star non-match regression and supplementary-code-point coverage while retaining the existing newline cases.
